images.alt: A coiled rope, a clay curd pot and a wooden mortar in a sunlit Gokula courtyard
images.caption: The objects that carry the story from Yashoda’s kitchen to the courtyard.
images.prompt: An original devotional still life in warm indigo and terracotta. Use a clay curd pot with a small crack, a coil of rope and a wooden mortar in a simple sunlit courtyard, with marigold petals in the foreground.

images.sectionHeading: Why was the rope always two fingers short?
images.alt: Two lengths of rope end on either side of a marked gap of two fingerbreadths
images.caption: The gap stays the same even as Yashoda joins more rope.
images.prompt: An original close-up diagram of two natural rope ends framing the label Two fingerbreadths, with discreet measure ticks. Emphasize the separation visually and keep the lettering large enough for small screens.

images.sectionHeading: What happened to the two arjuna trees?
images.alt: Two trees frame the wooden mortar caught crosswise between their trunks
images.caption: Bhagavata Purana 10.10 describes the mortar turning crosswise between the trees.
images.prompt: An original book illustration of twin arjuna trees in a moonlit green courtyard with the wooden mortar crosswise at their base. A rope leads out of frame, keeping focus on the passage through the trees.
